title: dequant budget simulator for adaptive pathing
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build a deterministic simulator that models per-request dequantization cost (latency and memory traffic) across mixed-precision and int8/fp8 kernel paths and expose a dequant budget metric to the kernel selection layer. The simulator will let the scheduler estimate when dequantization overhead outweighs precision benefits and select a precision-escape or passthrough path. This helps reduce tail latency regressions and token-level cost spikes for streaming and prefill workloads.
motivation: Existing kernel selector uses coarse heuristics for choosing mixed-precision vs full-precision paths and often underestimates dequant overhead for long-prefix prefill requests and cached KV reuse scenarios. This causes suboptimal path choices that increase latency and token cost. A lightweight simulator will produce a per-request expected dequant overhead estimate and a recommended precision decision to feed into routing policies and autoscale scoring.
scope: Simulation engine, an API to query per-request dequant budget, instrumentation hooks in the prefill/decode scheduler to consume the budget signal, a small dashboard to visualize dequant budget distribution, and unit/e2e tests against synthetic workloads.
out_of_scope: Rewriting kernel implementations or adding new quant kernels. Full model reprofiling pipelines are out of scope for this ticket (they will be a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulator produces per-request dequant_latency_ms and dequant_bandwidth_bytes estimates with <=15% median error vs microbenchmarks for representative models.
- Scheduler consumes simulator output and can switch route for mixed-precision iff expected dequant overhead > configured threshold.
- No per-request CPU overhead > 0.25ms added in the hot path (measurement on p4d-equivalent).
- Integration tests demonstrating latency tail (P95/P99) improvement on a synthetic prefilling workload when budget-aware routing is enabled.
- Dashboard shows historical distribution and explains decisions for at least 7 days of synthetic load data.
design_notes:
Approach: instrument microbenchmarks that measure: dequant per-token latency (for head groups), memory copy bandwidth implications, and KV cache amortization factors. Build a parametric model: dequant_cost = alpha * tokens + beta * heads + gamma * kv_misses + delta * batch_merges. Fit parameters from a small set of per-model calibrations. Keep simulator deterministic and lightweight so it can run in the scheduler process or as an offloaded sidecar. Provide two modes: fast approximate (use precomputed params) and debug mode (run microbench on-the-fly).
Key trade-offs: accuracy vs. runtime cost. We prioritize a conservative overestimate to avoid choosing slower paths. To avoid data explosion, we aggregate by request signature hash and maintain an LRU cache of estimates.
Telemetry: expose estimate_reason and fallback_signal to allow post-hoc analysis of path decisions.
implementation_plan:
1) Define simulator interface and proto (input: model_id, seq_len_prefix, num_heads, kv_hit_rate_est, batch_size; output: dequant_latency_ms, dequant_bytes, confidence_score, recommended_action).
2) Implement microbenchmark harness and run across representative models (gpt-3.5-sized, Llama-2-13B, and an fp8-optimized small model).
3) Fit model parameters and store baseline param bundles per model.
4) Implement simulator library in runtime (Rust component) with both approximate and debug modes.
5) Hook simulator call into prefill scheduler path decision code (fast path uses cached estimates).
6) Add feature flag runtime.dequant_budget_routing to enable/disable.
7) Add unit tests, microbenchmark tests, and e2e synthetic workload tests.
8) Create a small console view showing per-route budget utilization and decision traces.
9) Rollout behind feature flag to staging; run A/B test for 72h and evaluate P95/P99 and token cost metrics.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for simulator math and caching behavior.
- Integration tests that simulate KV-hit/miss scenarios and check correctness of decision flips.
- Performance tests to measure added overhead in the scheduler hot path (target <0.25ms).
- Calibration test suite that verifies fitted parameters against microbenchmark measurements within 15%.
- A/B e2e test on staging with 5K concurrent sessions for 72 hours comparing default vs budget-aware routing.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1: feature-flagged deploy to staging cluster; collect telemetry for 72h.
Stage 2: enable for 10% of traffic in canary region with auto rollback if P99 latency regresses >5% or token cost increases >3%.
Stage 3: expand to 50% then 100% after verification.
Fallback: runtime.dequant_budget_routing=false will always choose the existing heuristic path.
risks: Added runtime overhead that degrades hot-path latency
Incorrect KV hit estimates leading to wrong decisions
Edge cases for very short-lived sessions where caching of estimates misleads the scheduler
mitigations: Feature flag & canary with automatic rollback
Validate KV hit heuristics with sampled real traffic traces
LRU cache eviction and time-based TTL for estimates
security_considerations: Simulator reads only model metadata and request shape; must not log customer prompt content. Ensure no PII sent to calibration service. Access to parameter bundles controlled by runtime config RBAC.
updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with runtime and scheduler owners. Decided on two-mode design (approx/debug). Assigned initial benchmarks.

2025-02-25: Microbenchmark harness implemented. First runs on llama-2-13B show dequant per-token ~0.18ms for head groups with 16 heads. Saved raw traces to gs://redwood-perf/eng/eng-995001/trace-20250225.tar.gz.
2025-03-01: Parameter fitting completed for three models. Early simulator agrees with microbenchmarks median error 12%. Implemented Rust library skeleton and perf-tested library initialization cost.

2025-03-04: Hooked simulator into prefill scheduler in staging behind feature flag. Observed negligible added CPU on scheduler (~0.12ms per request) when using cached estimates. Enabled debug mode for sampled requests.
2025-03-05: Added console mockup for dequant budget distribution. Preparing canary rollout checklist and PRs.
notes: Follow-up tickets planned: a) automated per-model calibration pipeline, b) combine budget signal with autoscaler score, c) experiment with headwise partial dequant escape policies.
